account: Today I have repeatedly heard an unusual but vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 21 said baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour were there, and also reported that the innkeeper carried a sack of hay blocks at the mill. Other townsfolk repeated the bridge-or-port phrase without explaining it. I have not witnessed any change, established what was proposed, or learned its purpose. It might concern transport or deliveries, but that is only a possibility, not something I know. I sought the baker for clarification, but nobody answered and the bakery was empty when I checked around 10:40. My scheduled ten o'clock grain inspection also found no responsible mill staff. The secretary had already warned that the inspection was unconfirmed after unsuccessful attempts to find staff. I saw seventy-six hay bales and 104 emeralds in the mill stall, but found no records establishing deliveries, shortages or storage problems. I cannot conclude that the grain stock or the innkeeper's reported hay transport is connected to the bakery discussion. I have now returned to the office for the thirteen o'clock council letters and asked the secretary for correspondence and reliable details. I am awaiting an answer. Tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage is scheduled for fifteen; that may provide an opportunity to ask about the reported discussion directly.
